notes_list.title: Friedel–Crafts Alkylation and Acylation
notes_list.basic_overview: Electrophilic aromatic substitution introduces alkyl or acyl groups onto aromatic rings using Lewis-acid activation.
notes_list.extra_info_content: Alkylation can rearrange because carbocation-like electrophiles are involved; acylation gives an acylium ion and generally avoids rearrangement, then the aryl ketone can be reduced if an alkylbenzene is desired.
notes_list.examples: Benzene + CH3Cl/AlCl3 → toluene; benzene + RCOCl/AlCl3 → aryl ketone.
notes_list.conditions_and_medium: Dry Lewis-acid conditions; acyl chlorides/anhydrides with AlCl3 are common. Strongly deactivated rings may not react.
notes_list.mechanism_steps: Electrophile generation → aromatic π attack → σ-complex → deprotonation and aromaticity restoration.
notes_list.kinetics_and_energy: EAS rate is governed by electrophile generation and aromatic-ring nucleophilicity. Alkyl groups activate the ring and can promote polyalkylation.
notes_list.common_traps: Alkylation rearrangement and polyalkylation are classic traps; acylation is usually monoacylation because the carbonyl deactivates the ring.

exam_focus.level: IIT-JAM / MSc entrance / GATE concept depth
